rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> Hydrus-2d simulations plus greenhouse lysimeter experiments (bare soil and sweet corn) on Kidman sandy loam with buried drip emitters applying P-laden water continuously or every 2 d. Q2: Abstract and 'Distribution of plant-available P <U+2013> no uptake' (Fig. 5) <U+2013> bicarbonate-extractable P around the emitter was 20<U+2013>25% higher under continuous than pulsed drip fertigation; Conclusion <U+2013> continuous application gave greater P mobility and higher soil-solution P around emitters. Q3: Soil Olsen-P extraction on bare-soil lysimeters (Fig. 5) and, in the cropped experiment, plant tissue P plus a P mass balance (45% vs 27% of applied P in plant tissue) both indicate greater P availability under continuous application; authors state the tissue-P difference indicates P was more available when applied continuously. Q4: Fig. 5 and Fig. 3 <U+2013> gravimetric water content measured (tensiometers, soil sampling) and simulated; soil around emitters was wetter in the continuous treatment, the moisture condition through which P stays in solution and mobile. Q8: 'Comparison of simulation and lysimeter results' <U+2013> modelled (soluble) and measured (extractable) P not directly comparable; idealized soil ignoring variability, preferential flow and surfacing; Langmuir isotherm inadequate for P transport; and soil P differences were not evident when corn was grown with low P in irrigation water; Conclusion <U+2013> other crops and soil types still to be tested. Q9: Fig. 8 caption <U+2013> plant tissue P shown with standard deviations of replicates; Fig. 6 also SD bars for biomass.
rows.notes: Single soil (calcareous sandy loam), single crop, greenhouse lysimeters only. Triangulation accepted on soil extraction vs plant-uptake/mass-balance evidence; the Hydrus simulation used default parameters and was not validated against the lysimeter data, so it was not counted as an independent method on its own. Note the cropped experiment showed slightly lower soil extractable P under continuous fertigation (3.8 vs 4.3 mg/kg) even though uptake was higher. No support condition is stated as a requirement from own findings; the bare-soil/high-P vs cropped/low-P contrast is reported as a difference, not a condition. No dispersion given for the 20<U+2013>25% soil-P difference itself; SD only for plant variables.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own Hydrus-2d simulations and greenhouse lysimeter experiments with buried drip emitters, continuous vs 2-d pulsed fertigation on Kidman sandy loam. Q2: Abstract and Fig. 5 results <U+2013> Olsen bicarbonate-extractable P in soil immediately surrounding the point source was 20<U+2013>25% higher under continuous than pulsed fertigation on bare soil; Fig. 5 isocharts give the 2-D spatial distribution after 14 d. Q4: Fig. 5 and tensiometer monitoring <U+2013> measured water content distribution; soil around emitters was wetter under the continuous treatment, with the model (Fig. 3/4) showing stable wet zones holding P in solution. Q8: 'Comparison of simulation and lysimeter results' <U+2013> model and measurement not directly comparable (soluble vs extractable P), idealized soil representation, preferential flow/surfacing unaccounted, Langmuir sorption inadequate; 'Uptake of P by young corn' <U+2013> soil P distribution differences were not evident when corn was grown with low P concentration in the irrigation water.
rows.notes: Q3 no: the 20<U+2013>25% extractable-P result rests on one method (Olsen extraction of lysimeter soil samples, three replicates); the Hydrus simulation ran on default sandy-loam parameters, simulated soluble not extractable P, and the authors say the two are not directly comparable and distributions differed, so it is not treated as an independent confirming method. Q9 no: no SD, CI or replicate range is reported for the soil extractable-P difference; the ranges given (e.g. 4.0<U+2013>5.0 mg/kg) are spatial ranges across the profile, and SD bars are shown only for plant biomass and tissue P. Single soil, greenhouse lysimeters; the cropped experiment actually showed slightly lower extractable P under continuous fertigation, which qualifies the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a primary greenhouse lysimeter plus simulation study on one calcareous sandy loam with sweet corn; the claimed soil-P enhancement was found on bare soil with 70 mg P/L irrigation water but not in the cropped experiment with 7 mg P/L, where the benefit appeared as higher plant tissue P and biomass instead.
